# Process handles, formals and collections (SIM-015)

The task module runs every positive fixture through the public CLI in both HDL
optimizer modes on legacy, compact/portable and compact/GMP values (GMP when
`LLG_TEST_GMP_ROOT` is set). Expected outputs are derived by hand from the
cited clauses, not captured from llg. Status names follow the declaration
order of `process::state` (Annex G.6): `FINISHED`, `RUNNING`, `WAITING`,
`SUSPENDED`, `KILLED`, with ordinals 0 to 4.

A handle is the identity of its process (SV 9.7): copies in arrays, records,
class properties and formals name the same process, and the identity stays
valid after the process terminates for as long as any reference holds it.

| Fixture | Clause and independent oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `collections` | §§9.7, 7.4-7.10, 13.5. Child `k` (0..4) stores `self()` into a fixed, dynamic, queue, integral-key and string-key array and waits `10*(k+1)`. At 1 all five wait (`t1 k* WAITING`, read through the output formal of `pick`). Through an input formal: suspend k0 and k1, kill k2 (`fixed SUSPENDED`, `dyn SUSPENDED`, `queue KILLED`). At 15 k0's delay has passed while suspended, so it is still `SUSPENDED`; resume schedules it in the current step and `await` returns at 15 with `done[0]=1`. k1 resumes before its delay ends: `WAITING`. Awaiting k3 returns at 40. k4 is suspended and killed at 40. Final states `FINISHED FINISHED KILLED FINISHED KILLED`, `done 1 1 0 1 0`. |
| `formals` | §§13.3-13.5, 9.7. `g` waits until 100. By value: status 2 (`WAITING`). The output copies `g` out (`output 1`). The inout formal sees a waiting process and nulls the caller's copy (`inout 1 1`). A `ref` formal written with `self()` names the caller, which is running (`ref 1 RUNNING`). A function returns its handle formal (`return 1`); a `const ref` formal reads it (`const_ref 1`). A static task keeps its formal in static storage across its `#0` and reads it the same way (`static WAITING`). Killing through a `ref` formal kills the process `a` also names (`killed KILLED KILLED`); afterwards `const_ref 0` and `stage 0` (the killed process never reached `stage = 1`). |
| `members` | §§8.4, 7.2, 6.8 Table 6-7, 9.7. Defaults are null (`defaults 1 1 null`). The child stores itself into a class property and a record member. A record copy, a queue element, a static local record and an alias class handle all name it (`same 1 1 1 1`); a by-value record formal reads `rec 7 WAITING`. Suspending through the alias is seen through the record and another property (`suspended SUSPENDED SUSPENDED`); killing through the queue element is seen through the class and the local copy (`killed KILLED KILLED`). Nulling `r.p` leaves the copy's handle (`cleared 1 1`). |
| `wait_kinds` | §§9.7, 9.6.1, 15.3, 15.4. Seven children wait on a delay (until 10), a named event, `wait fork` (child ends at 8), a semaphore, a mailbox, `t_h.await()` and a second semaphore. At 1 all wait, then all are suspended. At 2 a key and message arrive while `s` and `m` are suspended: both stay `SUSPENDED`; the suspended `k` is killed and the key put to `sem_k` is still available (`try_get` 1). Resuming `s` at 3 and `m` at 4 finds the condition true: `s done 3`, `m done 4 got 42`. `t` and `e` resume at 5 before their conditions hold: `WAITING`. `->ev` at 6: `e done 6`. At 9 `f`'s child has ended while `f` was suspended: `SUSPENDED`, then resume: `f done 9`. `t done 10`. At 11 `a`'s target has finished but `a` is suspended; resume and await: `a done 11`. |
| `terminal_cases` | §9.7. A process kills itself at 1, which also kills its forked descendant: neither adds to `marks` (`self-kill KILLED KILLED marks=0`). Kill, suspend and resume of a finished process have no effect (`finished FINISHED`); `await` on finished and killed processes returns at once (`await terminal ok 2`). A second suspend has no effect (`SUSPENDED`); one resume before the delay ends gives `WAITING`; a second resume and second kill change nothing (`KILLED`). `marks=0` at the end. |
| `shared_handles` | §§9.3.2, 9.7, 13.5.1. `watch` reads its by-value formal in a fork branch at 3, while `w` waits until 5: `watch WAITING at 3`. In `run`, the sibling branch reads the task's process variable at 4 and kills the other branch, so `join` completes at 4: `sibling sees WAITING`, `run KILLED at 4`. |
| `randstate` | §§18.13-18.14. Seeding and snapshotting other processes does not touch the caller's stream (`caller stream unchanged 1`). Restoring `worker`'s state replays its draws (`restored 1`); `twin`, seeded with the same value, draws the same sequence (`same seed 1`). |
| `teardown` | §9.7. Four waiters store themselves into a class queue, a record queue and a process queue and fork a descendant; another child finishes at once. At 1 the first waiter is suspended, the second killed (with its descendant) and the third awaited by a child that never returns. Copies stay readable: `held 4 4 4`, `states FINISHED KILLED SUSPENDED WAITING`, `ids 1 1`. The model then ends with suspended, killed and finished targets, a pending await and live descendants; the sanitizer runs cover the teardown. |
| `handle_events` | §§9.7, 9.4.3, 15.4. The SV 9.7 `do_n_way` example (with a constant `N`, as `process job[1:N]` needs a constant range) waits until every job stored its handle, awaits job 1 (`job 1 done 10`) and kills the others (`do_n_way KILLED KILLED 10`). At 63 a child stores itself into `p`, which wakes `wait (p != null)` (`seen at 63`), and puts its handle into an untyped and a typed mailbox: `peek` and `get` return the same handle and a class property receives the typed copy (`mailbox 1 1 0`). `@(p)` wakes when `p` is nulled at 68 (`p changed at 68 null=1`); a `ref` formal rebinds `p` at 71 (`rebound at 71 1`). |
| `process_randstate` | Adopted FND-002 witness (ledger L-F12-05-03); its expected line is the witness's `Expected:` header; the copy ends with a quiet `$finish(0)`. |
| `wake_kill` | §§9.7, 4.7 (permitted set). `->go` wakes the victim; the triggering process kills it before it runs, so it never prints (`victim KILLED`), unless the implementation interleaves after the trigger, in which case it prints and finishes first (`victim ran`, `victim FINISHED`). `->pair` wakes `a` and `b` in an unspecified order; whichever runs first kills the other before it resumes (`a woke`, `pair FINISHED KILLED`, or the mirror). |
| `neg_null_await` | §§8.4, 9.7. A method call through a null handle is a null object access: the runtime reports `null process handle access: process::await` and ends the simulation (exit 1) without running the next statement. |
| `neg_self_await` | §9.7: "it shall be an error to call this task on the current process". The runtime reports it and ends the simulation (exit 1). |
| `neg_randstate_terminated` | §18.14. A terminated process owns no random stream; `srandom` through its retained handle reports an error (exit 1) and has no other effect; its status is still `FINISHED`. |
| `neg_ref_property` | Legal by §13.5.2 (a class property may be passed by reference); a `ref` process formal binds only counted process variables, so this is rejected explicitly. |
| `neg_expression_output` | Legal by §13.5; an output process formal bound to a process variable needs a copy-back statement, which a call inside an expression cannot run, so this is rejected explicitly. |
| `neg_status_wait` | Legal by §9.7; a status change publishes no change event, so a wait whose condition reads `status()` would never wake. It is rejected explicitly; `await()` waits for termination. |
| `neg_mailbox_try_get` | Legal by §15.4; `try_get` into a process variable needs a counted copy-back that an expression cannot run, so it is rejected explicitly (`get` and `peek` work). |
